page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n4d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 classifies this instance as a compute-optimized resource. Because there is no bundled local storage, all storage operations must rely on external network-attached block storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without the performance variability associated with shared-core or burstable instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-highcpu-4 offers a lean hardware profile designed for workloads that require dedicated processing power but have low memory footprints. This resource density is suitable for compute-heavy tasks such as lightweight web serving, build systems, CI/CD pipelines, and basic computational modeling where large memory arrays or local NVMe drives are not required.
